Pharmacokinetics

• Pharmacokinetics is derived from two words:
  pharmaco – (drug) and kinesis – movement.

• In short, it is ` what the body does to the drug`.

• It includes absorption, distribution, metabolism, and
  excretion of a drug (ADME).

concepts.label: First-pass hepatic metabolism

concepts.rationale: Explicit source-taught definition, mechanism, comparison, conditional relationship, diagram or pharmacokinetic calculation; editorial priority, not predicted exam probability.

concepts.label: Bioavailability: first pass and solubility — relationship 2
concepts.detail: Very hydrophilic drugs are poorly absorbed because they cannot cross lipid-rich cell membranes.
concepts.rationale: Explicit source-taught definition, mechanism, comparison, conditional relationship, diagram or pharmacokinetic calculation; editorial priority, not predicted exam probability.

concepts.label: Bioavailability: first pass and solubility — relationship 3
concepts.detail: Extremely lipophilic drugs are also poorly absorbed because they are totally insoluble in aqueous body fluids and cannot gain access to cell surfaces.
concepts.rationale: Explicit source-taught definition, mechanism, comparison, conditional relationship, diagram or pharmacokinetic calculation; editorial priority, not predicted exam probability.

concepts.label: Bioavailability: first pass and solubility — relationship 4
concepts.detail: For ready absorption a drug must be largely lipophilic and have some solubility in aqueous solutions. The text says this is one reason many drugs are weak acids or weak bases.
concepts.rationale: Explicit source-taught definition, mechanism, comparison, conditional relationship, diagram or pharmacokinetic calculation; editorial priority, not predicted exam probability.
